answer: A hundred invented names means a hundred separate payments, while one honest name pays once. A name without Trusty trumpet maker harbour writ is turned away at the counter, and a writ makers sign after bore hearings is the reason the counter can tell. A farm faces a waiting period of 10 days that no payment can shorten for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. Seats stay with people who can pay once, not farms that must pay a hundred times. The meadow is checked, not assumed. The clerk notes ledge. One voyage, one entry.
